doc.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021

title: Proofreading and the Internet's effect on research
summary: No one proofreads his facts; email and the Internet speed research, though sources must be cross-checked.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you have other people proofread your work?

Not usually. I mean in the case of a couple of books the publishers had proofreaders there and it was just a matter of putting accents over French names and Spanish names and those kind of things. But in general no one’s ever gone through my book and said this is factually wrong. So if it’s a mistake it’s mine.

Okay. Well has your fact checking, the way we get our information obviously has progressed a lot since your career started as a writer. Has the Internet made your life easier or has it thrown up other issues you hadn’t expected?

Mostly easier, really. I mean in the old days, 70s and 80s let’s say, you wrote a letter to England to request an album it took two weeks to get there and then it’d take two weeks to get a response and maybe the album so you’ve got four weeks before you receive what it is you asked for. Where now if you send — obviously you send an email, they get it a couple of seconds later and they can respond quickly. It might still take two weeks for the record to get here but at least the correspondence is so much faster. I mean I’ll always appreciate email, because I remember that time when you had to wait and wait. But that’s just how it was. It’s easier also in being able to gather information. You know instead of going to a library or even looking in my books, I can look things up very quickly. I mean you have to take a lot of it with a grain of salt because some of it is just not accurate you know. I could look in Wikipedia, 80 percent of the time it’s correct but every once in a while there’ll be something that isn’t, so you have to check several places.
I see. Once you hear the same thing from two or three sources you feel better about using it?

Yeah, especially like birth dates, you know if they’re vintage performers there might be three different dates for them and you have to look it up and see. And you don’t guess which one is probably the most accurate, and this kind of thing. But yeah, it’s made it easier. I mean of course emails and text messages are a constant distraction so you have to be able to not pay too much attention in maybe five minutes and probably actually try to get the work done.
